Founded in 1892 as a literary and cycling club, they are the second most successful club in the [[Czech Republic]] since its independence in 1993.{{cite web|title=Historická tabulka|url=https://www.chanceliga.cz/tabulka/2019/historicka|work=Chance Liga|access-date=10 June 2019}} They play in the [[Czech First League]], the top division in the [[Czech Republic]]. They play the [[Prague derby]] with [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]], the most prominent rivalry in Czech football. Slavia has won 22 league titles, 11 Czech cups, and the [[Mitropa Cup]] in 1938. The club has won nine league titles since the foundation of the Czech league in 1993. They have also reached the semi-finals of the [[1995–96 UEFA Cup]] and qualified for the [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League group stage]] for the first time in their history. In 2019, Slavia reached the quarter-finals of the [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League]] and also qualified for the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League group stage]] for the second time in their history. They once again reached the Europa League quarter-finals in [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|2020–21]]. In the title-winning [[2020–21 Czech First League]] season the team completed an entire season undefeated and set a Czech record for the longest top-flight unbeaten league run at 54 games between 2020 and 2021.{{cite web|title=NEPORAŽENÍ 582 dnů. Série, na kterou se nezapomene|url=https://www.slavia.cz/clanek.asp?id=18766|publisher=SK Slavia Prague|access-date=17 October 2021|archive-date=17 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211017152807/https://www.slavia.cz/clanek.asp?id=18766|url-status=live}} In addition to their men's squad, Slavia Prague has two reserves ([[SK Slavia Prague B]] and SK Slavia Prague C), youth, and [[SK Slavia Prague (women)|women's]] teams. ==History== Slavia Prague was founded on 2 November 1892{{#tag:ref|In 2020, the Odbor přátel (coalition of fan organisations) has uncovered that the club was actually established on 14 November 1892, the traditional date being erroneously reported in the year 1902 by an article commemorating 10 and then repeated from this article.|group="nb"|name="zalozeni"}} by medicine students in [[Vinohrady]], [[Prague]], as a literary and cycling club. The club soon ceased to exist and a new one was founded in 1895. The new club initially focused on [[Cycle sport|cycling]], and expanded to football in 1896.{{cite web|last=Běrný|first=Aleš|title=Přesně před 120 lety založili studenti Slavii, klub funguje dodnes|url=https://www.idnes.cz/praha/zpravy/slavia-slavi-120-let.A121102_1849108_praha-zpravy_ab|work=iDNES.cz|date=2 November 2012|access-date=27 November 2025|language=cs|archive-date=27 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127030043/http://praha.idnes.cz/slavia-slavi-120-let-039-/praha-zpravy.aspx?c=A121102_1849108_praha-zpravy_ab|url-status=live}} On 25 March of that year, Slavia won their first match against AC Prague 5–0. The captain of this team was [[Karel Freja]]. Four days later, Slavia played against [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]], with the match finishing 0–0, this match being the start of the rivalry between these two clubs.{{cite web|title=Historie Zápasů – 1896|url=http://www.slavia.cz/zobraz.asp?t=zapasy-1896|website=Slavia Prague|access-date=29 May 2014|language=cs|archive-date=11 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811083023/http://www.slavia.cz/zobraz.asp?t=zapasy-1896|url-status=live}}{{cite web|title=O derby. Proč a jak dlouho se nemáme rádi|url=http://www.sparta.cz/novinky/zpravodajstvi/a-tym/o-derby-proc-a-jak-dlouho-se-nemame-radi-5518.html|website=Sparta Prague|access-date=29 May 2014|language=cs|archive-date=9 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809220403/http://www.sparta.cz/novinky/zpravodajstvi/a-tym/o-derby-proc-a-jak-dlouho-se-nemame-radi-5518.html|url-status=dead}} [[File:Slavia Praha 1901.png|thumb|SK Slavia Prague team in 1901]] In 1905, [[Scotland|Scottish]] manager and former [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] player [[Johnny Madden]] brought new tactics and views on football from his home country to the club. He managed to set up an early golden age for the club that lasted 25 years. Under Madden Slavia won 134 domestic matches out of a total of 169, and 304 internationals out of 429 between 1905 and 1930. In 1930, Madden retired from Slavia and professional football at the age of 66, though he remained in Prague for the rest of his life. In the [[1934 FIFA World Cup|1934 World Cup]], the [[1934 FIFA World Cup squads#Czechoslovakia|Czechoslovak national team]] included eight Slavia players. The second golden period came when Slavia bought [[Josef Bican]] from [[VfB Admira Wacker Mödling|Admira Vienna]]. Slavia with Bican won titles in [[1939–40 Czechoslovak First League|1940]], [[1940–41 Czechoslovak First League|1941]], [[1941–42 Czechoslovak First League|1942]] and [[1942–43 Czechoslovak First League|1943]], while many football players were at war. In [[1951 Czechoslovak First League|1951]] Slavia finished in 11th position in the league. Poor results continued during the 1950s and 1960s when Slavia were relegated twice, in [[1960–61 Czechoslovak First League|1961]] and [[1962–63 Czechoslovak First League|1963]]. They next played in the top level of football in [[1965–66 Czechoslovak First League|1965]]. In 1996, Slavia won their 14th title after 49 years.{{cite book|first=Luboš|last=Jeřábek|title=Český a československý fotbal – lexikon osobností a klubů|publisher=Grada Publishing|language=cs|year=2007|location=Prague, Czech Republic|isbn=978-80-247-1656-5|page=163}} During this season, Slavia played in the semi-final of the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] and four players of this team had big importance for the silver medal-winning Czech team from [[UEFA Euro 1996]].{{Cite web|title=Statika|url=http://www.slavia.cz/statika.asp?typ=hEsej|url-status=dead|website=Slavia Prague|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070909135819/http://www.slavia.cz/statika.asp?typ=hEsej|archive-date=9 September 2007}} Slavia participated in the qualifying rounds for the [[UEFA Champions League]] five times ([[1996–97 UEFA Champions League|1996]], [[2000–01 UEFA Champions League|2000]], [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|2001]], [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|2004]] and [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League|2005]]), being eliminated each time until finally qualifying for the group stage in the [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League|2007–08 season]] following a 3–1 aggregate victory over [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] in the third qualifying round. For the group stage, Slavia were drawn in Group H along with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[FC Steaua București|Steaua București]] and [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. They started with a 2–1 win at home against Steaua and a 4–2 loss to Sevilla. Next came two matches against Arsenal; Slavia lost 7–0 at the [[Emirates Stadium]], but eventually draw 0–0 in the second leg. In [[Bucharest]] came a 1–1 draw, which qualified the Czech team for the UEFA Cup round of 32, from third place in Group H, in spite of a home 0–3 defeat against Sevilla. In October 2006, the construction of the new and long-awaited stadium at [[Eden Arena|Eden]] for 21,000 spectators began. The stadium was opened on 7 May 2008 with an [[Exhibition game#Association football|exhibition match]] against [[Oxford University A.F.C.|Oxford University]].{{cite web| title=Czech champions Slavia too strong for Blues| url=http://www.ouafc.com/news/262| access-date=13 November 2008| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081206161411/http://www.ouafc.com/news/262| archive-date=6 December 2008| df=dmy-all}} In the [[2007–08 Czech First League|2007–08]] and [[2008–09 Czech First League|2008–09]], Slavia were back-to-back Czech champions, but did not play in the Champions League group stage due to elimination in the qualifying rounds by [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] (0–2 on aggregate in 2008–09) and [[FC Sheriff Tiraspol|Sheriff Tiraspol]] (1–1 on [[away goals rule]] in 2009–10). In the [[2009–10 Czech First League]], the club managed only seventh place in the league. In the autumn of 2010, the club found itself in crisis due to its economic problems. It was discovered that Slavia owed 112 million [[Czech koruna]] to the club's former owner, [[ENIC Group|ENIC Sports Ltd]] (English National Investment Company).{{cite web|title=Konec sporů: Natland se dohodl se zástupci ENICu a uhradil dluhy Slavie|url=http://sport.ihned.cz/c1-52092650-konec-sporu-natland-se-dohodl-se-zastupci-enicu-a-uhradil-dluhy-slavie|website=[[Hospodářské noviny]]|date=15 June 2011|access-date=29 May 2014|language=cs|archive-date=10 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111010104435/http://sport.ihned.cz/c1-52092650-konec-sporu-natland-se-dohodl-se-zastupci-enicu-a-uhradil-dluhy-slavie|url-status=live}} As a result, major cost-cutting was needed to service this debt and it was confirmed that the squad needed to be purged. In addition to the players sold, midfielder [[Petr Trapp]] left the club mid-season, claiming that Slavia had not paid his wages for three months.{{cite web|title=Fotbalista Trapp se po dvou letech vrací ze Slavie zpátky do Plzně|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/fotbalista-trapp-se-po-dvou-letech-vraci-ze-slavie-zpatky-do-plzne-1cs-/fotbal.aspx?c=A110105_162023_fotbal_mn|website=[[Mladá fronta Company]] bought the team. From November 2018, the club was owned by the Sinobo Group and [[CITIC Group]]. Since December 2023, the club is owned by the Czech businessman [[Pavel Tykač]], who bought the club from its Chinese owners for a reported sum of 2 billion Czech crowns.{{cite news | title=Tykač koupil Slavii i Eden. "Z osobních důvodů", vzkázal | newspaper=Minutové Zprávy| date=21 December 2023 | url=https://minutovezpravy.cz/clanek/tykac-koupil-slavii-i-s-edenem/|access-date=7 March 2024|language=cs|archive-date=7 March 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240307090748/https://minutovezpravy.cz/clanek/tykac-koupil-slavii-i-s-edenem/ | url-status=live }} ==Historical names== * 1892 – '''SK ACOS Praha''' (Sportovní klub Akademický cyklistický odbor Slavia Praha) * 1893 – '''SK Slavia Praha''' (Sportovní klub Slavia Praha) * 1948 – '''Sokol Slavia Praha''' * 1949 – '''ZSJ Dynamo Slavia Praha''' (Základní sportovní jednota Dynamo Slavia Praha) * 1953 – '''DSO Dynamo Praha''' (Dobrovolná sportovní organizace Dynamo Praha) * 1954 – '''TJ Dynamo Praha''' (Tělovýchovná jednota Dynamo Praha) * 1965 – '''SK Slavia Praha''' (Sportovní klub Slavia Praha) * 1973 – '''TJ Slavia Praha''' (Tělovýchovná jednota Slavia Praha) * 1977 – '''TJ Slavia IPS Praha''' (Tělovýchovná jednota Slavia Inženýrské průmyslové stavby Praha) * 1978 – '''SK Slavia IPS Praha''' (Sportovní klub Slavia Inženýrské průmyslové stavby Praha) * 1991 – '''SK Slavia Praha''' (Sportovní klub Slavia Praha – fotbal, a.s.) ==Club symbols== [[File:Flag of SK Slavia Prague.svg|right|thumb|Flag of SK Slavia Prague.]] The club's colours, red and white, were chosen as standing for the heart and blood, and fair play and sportsmanship respectively. The inverted five-pointed star was intended to symbolise "new hope, forever strengthening the mind and uplifting the spirit." The name "Slavia" is a [[Latin language|Latin]] term used in older literature to denote the lands inhabited by [[Slavs]].{{cite book|last=Kollar|first=Jan|title=Sláwa bohyně a půwod gména Slawůw čili Slawjanůw}} ==Supporters and rivalries== Slavia's greatest rivals are [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]], with whom they contest the [[Prague derby]]. A local [[Vršovice]] derby is also contested between Slavia and [[Bohemians 1905]], whose stadium is situated a kilometre from Eden.{{cite web|title=A look ahead: Here comes SK Slavia Praha|url=http://www.union-berlin.com/2013/09/04/here-comes-sk-slavia-praha/|work=Union Berlin FC|access-date=29 May 2014|archive-date=21 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170221010939/http://union-berlin.com/2013/09/04/here-comes-sk-slavia-praha/|url-status=dead}} Slavia is widely misconceived as being a [[Jewish]] club among other fans, particularly Sparta fans, and its fans and players are often subjected to anti-semitic abuse. However, the club was not founded by Jews nor did it have any Jewish history. Football historian Vladimír Zapotocký commented in an interview that were this the case, the [[Nazis]] would have shut the club down during the wartime [[Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia|occupation]], as they did with [[DFC Prag]]. The association stems from a friendly match played against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in 1922, when Slavia insured the match against adverse weather conditions, and the match was later cancelled due to rain. They then agreed with West Ham to play the fixture the next day, while also collecting money from the insurance company for cancelling the fixture. A week later in a Prague derby fixture, Slavia were greeted onto the pitch by chants of "vy židi!" ("you Jews!") from the Sparta fans.{{cite web|title=ZAUJALO NÁS: Kde se vzal pokřik jude Slavie?|url=http://www.supporters.cz/clanek/zaujalo-nas-kde-se-vzal-pokrik-jude-slavie-/4567.html|work=Supporters.cz|access-date=29 May 2014|archive-date=29 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140529231452/http://www.supporters.cz/clanek/zaujalo-nas-kde-se-vzal-pokrik-jude-slavie-/4567.html|url-status=live}} Since 2021, there is a fan coalition with Sportowe Zagłębie ([[Zagłębie Sosnowiec]] hooligans).{{Cite web|url = http://hooligans.cz/domains/hooligans.cz/index.php/reports/czech/7727-bitka-slavia-praha-zaglebie-sosnowiec-vs-banik-ostrava-gks-katowice-spartak-trnava-pohled-sks|title = Bitka Slavia Praha + Zaglebie Sosnowiec vs Baník Ostrava + GKS Katowice + Spartak Trnava (pohled SKS)|date = 30 June 2021|access-date = 28 April 2023|archive-date = 28 April 2023|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230428142223/http://hooligans.cz/domains/hooligans.cz/index.php/reports/czech/7727-bitka-slavia-praha-zaglebie-sosnowiec-vs-banik-ostrava-gks-katowice-spartak-trnava-pohled-sks|url-status = live}} ==Cooperations== In May 2018 a strategic cooperation with Chinese club [[Beijing Sinobo Guoan]] for both professional and youth level football started.{{Cite web|url=http://www.radio.cz/en/section/news/slavia-prague-seals-cooperation-with-oldest-chinese-football-club|title = Slavia Prague seals cooperation with oldest Chinese football club|date = 19 April 2018}} And in 2025 a project Slavia d’Abidjan started in [[Abidjan]], Ivory Coast.{{Cite web |title=Slavia d’Abidjan. Klub podpoří projekt Simona Deliho |url=https://www.slavia.cz/article/23139-Slavia-d%E2%80%99Abidjan-Klub-podpori-projekt-Simona-Deliho |access-date=2026-05-30 |publisher=SK Slavia Prague}} Other famous players include forward [[Antonín Puč]], goalkeeper [[František Plánička]] (both of them members of the [[Czechoslovakia national football team|Czechoslovakia national team]] in two [[FIFA World Cup|World Cups]]) and midfielder [[František Veselý]]. Čínskou společnost Sinobo |access-date=21 March 2021 |archive-date=5 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220405033239/https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2018-19/350737/slavia-ma-oficialne-noveho-majoritniho-vlastnika-cinskou-spolecnost-sinobo.html |url-status=live}} which has on 11 November 2018 purchased a majority stake from [[CITIC Group|CITIC]], at the time holding 99.98% of the 212,074 stocks worth of CZK 1.514 billion (Annual report from 30 June 2018). CITIC remains to be a minority shareholder and the companies did not reveal the distribution of the shares. According to their chairman Jinhui Zhou, the Sinobo business model is a combination of real estate development and sports activities.{{Cite web|url=http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/201801/18/WS5a5ff1faa310e4ebf433e6e7.html|website=www.chinadaily.com.cn|title=Luxury apartment builder Sinobo to focus on mix-use projects|access-date=21 March 2021|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727101450/https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/201801/18/WS5a5ff1faa310e4ebf433e6e7.html|url-status=live}} In a similar business model, Sinobo owns 64% of the shares in the [[Chinese Super League|Chinese]] club [[Beijing Sinobo Guoan F.C.|Beijing Guoan]] where the 36% minority belongs to [[CITIC Limited|CITIC]]. Sinobo also holds the naming rights of the arena, the [[Sinobo Stadium]]. The Chinese investment activity in Slavia has firstly started in September 2005, when a private [[conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] [[CEFC China Energy|CEFC]] acquired 59.97% shares of the club through its Czech subsidiary CEFC Group (Europe) Company a.s. from [[Aleš Řebíček]] for CZK 27 million. Through the course of the years, the share has increased to 67% and 80%, and on 22 November 2016 CEFC has capitalised its loan into the equity and increased their shares to 99.96% which made them the sole owner. In early 2018, it turned out that CEFC had serious financial problems and CITIC bought the club and arena. In late 2018, CITIC transferred Slavia's majority stake to the Chinese company Sinobo Group. He replaced [[Jaroslav Šilhavý]], who was appointed in September 2016 and moved on to manage the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech national team]]. There have been 65 managers in Slavia's history. The club's first professional coach, [[Johnny Madden]], was appointed in 1905, serving in that position until 1930.
